key_insight: A video diffusion model can plausibly reconstruct lost HDR scene radiance from 8-bit LDR videos, enabling realistic re-exposure and recovery of highlight/shadow detail while preserving temporal coherence.
problem_solved: LDR videos stored in 8-bit formats lose highlight and shadow information due to saturation and quantization, making accurate re-exposure and HDR mapping impossible with prior expansion methods that fail to restore realistic detail and temporal consistency.
method: Train a video-aware diffusion model to predict plausible high dynamic range radiance from saturated/quantized LDR frames.
Condition generation on re‑exposure parameters so a single LDR sequence can be re-exposed to arbitrary luminance targets in post.
Enforce temporal consistency (e.g., frame conditioning or flow-aware priors) and perceptual reconstruction losses to avoid flicker and produce coherent HDR video.
impact: Enables ML practitioners and content creators to recover and re-expose archival or consumer LDR video into perceptually realistic HDR, improving downstream editing, display mapping, and restoration pipelines without specialized capture.
visual_elements: Before/after pair: LDR frame vs. reconstructed HDR re-exposed frame (side-by-side) with zoomed crops of highlight/shadow areas.
Interactive exposure slider mockup showing same video re-exposed to different luminance targets.
Model diagram: video diffusion pipeline with temporal conditioning and exposure-conditioning inputs.
Temporal consistency visualization: frame-difference heatmap or short GIF demonstrating flicker-free reconstruction across frames.
paper_title: DiffHDR: Re-Exposing LDR Videos with Video Diffusion Models
paper_authors: Zhengming Yu, Li Ma, Mingming He, Leo Isikdogan, Yuancheng Xu
